title: BNCI 2025-002 Continuous 2D Trajectory Decoding dataset
description: This dataset comprises continuous 2D trajectory decoding data from 10 participants (9 able-bodied and 1 with spinal cord injury) performing attempted arm/hand movements while EEG was recorded. Participants tracked visual targets (snake-run tasks) or traced shapes (free-run tasks) while their arm was restrained, with decoded trajectory feedback provided in 50% and 100% EEG feedback conditions. The dataset includes preprocessed 60-channel EEG data acquired at 200 Hz, suitable for regression-based motor decoding research and assessment of learning effects across three sessions.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 60 channels using an actiCAP system (Brain Products GmbH) at 200 Hz sampling rate with right mastoid reference and Fpz ground. Participants performed attempted lower arm/hand movements as if wielding a computer mouse while the arm was strapped to an armrest. The experimental protocol included calibration runs (snake-run target tracking and eye-run baseline) followed by online feedback sessions with 50% and 100% EEG feedback conditions. Data were preprocessed including anti-aliasing (25 Hz) and notch (50 Hz) filtering, downsampling to 100 Hz, bad channel interpolation, eye artifact subtraction (SGEYESUB), high-pass filtering (0.18 Hz), common average re-referencing, artifact attenuation (HEAR algorithm), low-pass filtering (3 Hz), and final downsampling to 20 Hz. Feature extraction employed temporal features and sLORETA source localization with PLS regression and UKF smoothing for trajectory decoding.
